tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from his test results?

options.A: It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life.
options.B: There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.
options.C: There is some indication of an issue with his blood circulation.
options.D: He doesn’t know he has long been suffering from poor health.

questions.cn: 从检查结果中我们了解到男士什么情况？

optionsCn.A: 显然他可以期待健康的生活。
optionsCn.B: 他的消化系统没有任何问题。
optionsCn.C: 有一些迹象表明他的血液循环有问题。
optionsCn.D: 他不知道自己的身体状况长期不佳。

questions.stem: What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people?

options.A: Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress.
options.B: Complaining they are being overworked.
options.C: Being unaware of the stress they are under.
options.D: Suffering from illness without recognising it.

questions.cn: 女士认为许多人中存在的一种普遍现象是什么？

optionsCn.A: 把疾病症状误认为压力。
optionsCn.C: 没有察觉到自己所承受的压力。
optionsCn.D: 患病却不知道。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she will do for the man?

options.A: Prescribe some medication for him.
options.B: Give him another physical check-up.
options.C: Explain to him the common consequence of stress.
options.D: Buy some sleeping pills for him from the drugstore.

questions.cn: 女士说她会为男士做什么？

optionsCn.A: 给他开一些药。
optionsCn.C: 向他解释压力的常见后果。
optionsCn.D: 去药店给他买些安眠药。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the industry he is engaged in?

options.A: It calls for responsible management.
options.B: It proves to be quite profitable.
options.C: It is remarkably promising.
options.D: It is full of competition.

questions.cn: 关于他所从事的行业，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它要求负责任的管理。
optionsCn.C: 它前景非常光明。
optionsCn.D: 它充满竞争。

lines.t: Hello, doctor.
lines.cn: 你好，医生。

lines.t: Hello, please take a seat.
lines.cn: 你好，请坐。

lines.t: I have your test results here, and it’s good news.
lines.cn: 你的检查结果在我这儿，是好消息。

lines.t: The blood test came back clear.
lines.cn: 血液检查结果正常。

lines.t: There is no indication of any digestive issues.
lines.cn: 没有任何消化系统问题的迹象。

lines.t: So then, why do I feel so poorly all the time?
lines.cn: 那我为什么一直感觉这么不舒服？

lines.t: It’s probably due to overwork and stress.
lines.cn: 这大概是因为过度劳累和压力。

lines.t: No, it can’t be.
lines.cn: 不，不可能。

lines.t: I’ve always been working hard, but I’ve never felt stress.
lines.cn: 我一直很拼命工作，但从没感觉到压力。

lines.t: Other people suffering complain about that, but I don’t.
lines.cn: 别的患者会抱怨压力，但我不会。

lines.t: It must be something else.
lines.cn: 一定是别的原因。

lines.t: What you have just described is a common sentiment.
lines.cn: 你刚才描述的是一种很常见的感受。

lines.t: Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it.
lines.cn: 许多受压力困扰的人都没能察觉到自己有压力。

lines.t: You told me you often work long into the night, right?
lines.cn: 你告诉过我你常常工作到深夜，对吧？

lines.t: Yes, most days, in fact.
lines.cn: 是的，事实上大多数日子都是。

lines.t: But I’ve been doing that for about 20 years now.
lines.cn: 但我这样已经大约 20 年了。

lines.t: That doesn’t matter.
lines.cn: 那没关系。

lines.t: You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it.
lines.cn: 你可能已经受压力困扰 20 年而毫不自知。

lines.t: And now it’s catching up to you.
lines.cn: 现在它开始找上你了。

lines.t: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?
lines.cn: 但我一直觉得累、晚上也睡不好，这又怎么解释？

lines.t: Those are common consequences of stress.
lines.cn: 这些都是压力的常见后果。

lines.t: And if you don’t sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued.
lines.cn: 而如果你睡不好，当然就会感到疲惫。

lines.t: I’m going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you.
lines.cn: 我给你开一些特别的安眠药。

lines.t: They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients.
lines.cn: 它们作用温和，由天然成分制成。

lines.t: So your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn’t be any negative side effects.
lines.cn: 所以你的胃应该能耐受，也不会有任何不良副作用。

lines.t: Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month.
lines.cn: 晚饭时吃一粒，一个月后来找我。

lines.t: If there is no improvement, I’ll give you something stronger.
lines.cn: 如果没有改善，我再给你药效更强的。

lines.t: Thank you, doctor.
lines.cn: 谢谢你，医生。

lines.t: That’s not all.
lines.cn: 还有一点。

lines.t: You should try and work less.
lines.cn: 你应该试着少干点活。

lines.t: Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
lines.cn: 有没有办法减少你的工作量？

lines.t: Um, I’d have to think about it.
lines.cn: 呃，我得想想。

lines.t: I’m a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive.
lines.cn: 我是餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。

lines.t: There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
lines.cn: 有很多事情要跟、要盯住。

lines.t: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else.
lines.cn: 我建议你考虑把一些职责分派给别人。

lines.t: I’m not asking you to retire, just to slow down a bit.
lines.cn: 我不是让你退休，只是稍微放慢一点。

lines.t: It’s for your own health.
lines.cn: 这是为了你自己的健康。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why did John Williams leave the sport of basketball at just 25?

options.A: To avoid being in the limelight.
options.B: To seek medical help for his injury.
options.C: To pursue a less competitive career.
options.D: To stay away from his hostile teammates.

questions.cn: 约翰·威廉姆斯为什么 25 岁就离开篮球运动？

optionsCn.A: 为了不再备受瞩目。
optionsCn.C: 为了从事竞争较小的职业。
optionsCn.D: 为了远离对他有敌意的队友。

questions.stem: What does the man say about basketball as a career for most players?

options.A: It has ups and downs.
options.B: It proves rewarding.
options.C: It does not last long.
options.D: It is not so profitable.

questions.cn: 关于篮球作为大多数球员的职业，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它有起有落。
optionsCn.C: 它持续不了多久。
optionsCn.D: 它赚不了多少钱。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the woman about John Williams 20 years later?

options.A: He was a financial advisor.
options.B: He suffered from poor health.
options.C: He became a basketball coach.
options.D: He was back in the news.

questions.cn: 20 年后，从女士的话中我们了解到约翰·威廉姆斯什么？

optionsCn.A: 他是一名理财顾问。
optionsCn.C: 他成了篮球教练。
optionsCn.D: 他又回到了新闻里。

questions.stem: What has the man spent the last two decades trying to do?

options.A: Study issues of public health.
options.B: Alleviate the obesity problem.
options.C: Raise sufficient public funding.
options.D: Train young basketball players.

questions.cn: 过去二十年，男士一直在努力做什么？

optionsCn.A: 研究公共卫生问题。
optionsCn.C: 筹集充足的公共资金。
optionsCn.D: 训练年轻篮球运动员。

lines.t: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams.
lines.cn: 今天《新闻人物》的嘉宾是约翰·威廉姆斯。

lines.t: The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player.
lines.cn: 这个名字你可能不熟悉，但约翰曾是广受赞誉的篮球运动员。

lines.t: John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25.
lines.cn: 约翰，你在 25 岁就离开这项运动，让球迷们大为震惊。

lines.t: Why did you retire so early?
lines.cn: 你为什么这么早就退役？

lines.t: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn’t love being a celebrity.
lines.cn: 梅格，我喜欢当运动员，但我不喜欢当名人。

lines.t: I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake.
lines.cn: 我还在读高中时就备受瞩目，高中一毕业就转职业，那是个错误。

lines.t: I was a shy kid and I wasn’t ready for all the media attention.
lines.cn: 我是个害羞的孩子，还没准备好应对媒体的种种关注。

lines.t: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career?
lines.cn: 但在事业巅峰期放弃数百万美元？

lines.t: Most people wouldn’t be able to resist the lure of such a high salary.
lines.cn: 大多数人抵挡不住如此高薪的诱惑。

lines.t: When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.
lines.cn: 你离开这项运动时，外界猜测你和队友有矛盾，甚至是受了伤。

lines.t: Not at all.
lines.cn: 完全不是。

lines.t: It was hard to quit.
lines.cn: 退出很难。

lines.t: I was tempted to stay in the game, because I loved basketball and I loved my team.
lines.cn: 我很想留在赛场上，因为我爱篮球，也爱我的球队。

lines.t: As for money, I turned professional at 18, so I’d actually earned a lot and saved most of it because I had great financial advisors.
lines.cn: 至于钱，我 18 岁就转职业，所以其实挣了很多，而且因为有出色的理财顾问，大部分都存了下来。

lines.t: I knew basketball wasn’t a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
lines.cn: 我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球不是能长久从事的职业，所以我想趁还年轻就转行。

lines.t: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you’re back in the news.
lines.cn: 好，那已经是 20 年前的事了，而你又回到了新闻里。

lines.t: You’ve created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports.
lines.cn: 你创办了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。

lines.t: Why?
lines.cn: 为什么？

lines.t: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities.
lines.cn: 我上大学时学的是公共卫生，了解到肥胖流行的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的孩子和青少年中。

lines.t: I’ve spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem.
lines.cn: 过去二十年我一直在努力缓解这个问题。

lines.t: The foundation is just the latest attempt.
lines.cn: 这个基金会只是最新的尝试。

lines.t: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?
lines.cn: 该基金会用私人捐款资助小学男女生篮球队，对吧？

lines.t: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students too, and also have some public funding.
lines.cn: 其实，我们也资助中学生球队，而且还有一些公共资金。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women’s magazines?

options.A: When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland.
options.B: While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature.
options.C: After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum.
options.D: After winning the 1986 Woman’s Own Short Story Competition.

questions.cn: 凯特·阿特金森何时开始为女性杂志撰稿？

optionsCn.A: 当她在苏格兰爱丁堡大学开始任教时。
optionsCn.B: 当她在攻读美国文学博士时。
optionsCn.C: 在出版第一部小说《博物馆幕后》之后。
optionsCn.D: 在赢得 1986 年《Woman's Own》短篇小说大赛之后。

questions.stem: What did Kate Atkinson’s books touch on?

options.A: The themes of love and loss.
options.B: The code of human behaviour.
options.C: The sins and flaws of eccentrics.
options.D: The manners of fashionable circles.

questions.cn: 凯特·阿特金森的书触及什么？

optionsCn.A: 爱与失去的主题。
optionsCn.C: 怪人的罪与缺陷。
optionsCn.D: 时髦圈子的礼节。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners?

options.A: They are usually ignorant of complex human relations.
options.B: They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities.
options.C: They often get rewarded instead of being punished.
options.D: They are generally looked down upon in society.

questions.cn: 关于风俗喜剧中聪明而诡诈的角色，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们通常对复杂的人际关系一无所知。
optionsCn.B: 他们成功模仿名流的礼节。
optionsCn.C: 他们往往得到奖赏而不是惩罚。
optionsCn.D: 他们在社会上通常被人看不起。

lines.t: Kate Atkinson was born in York, England, in 1951.
lines.cn: 凯特·阿特金森 1951 年生于英格兰约克。

lines.t: She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author.
lines.cn: 她为获得作家的资质付出了艰苦努力。

lines.t: She studied English Literature at university in Scotland.
lines.cn: 她在苏格兰上大学时学的是英国文学。

lines.t: After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature.
lines.cn: 1974 年毕业后，她研究美国文学攻读博士学位。

lines.t: Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981.
lines.cn: 后来，她在自己毕业的大学任教，并于 1981 年开始写短篇小说。

lines.t: She began writing for women’s magazines after winning the 1986 Woman’s Own Short Story Competition.
lines.cn: 在赢得 1986 年《Woman's Own》短篇小说大赛后，她开始为女性杂志撰稿。

lines.t: Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year Award.
lines.cn: 她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》获得了 1995 年英国年度图书奖。

lines.t: The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV.
lines.cn: 这本书以约克郡为背景，已被改编为广播、戏剧和电视剧。

lines.t: She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh- the first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.
lines.cn: 她为爱丁堡的一家剧院写了两部剧——第一部叫《Nice》，第二部叫《遗弃》，于 2000 年 8 月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分上演。

lines.t: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.
lines.cn: 无论阿特金森写哪种体裁，她的书都触及爱与失去、以及如何继续前行这些主题。

lines.t: They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor.
lines.cn: 它们总是以机巧和一种顽皮的幽默感呈现。

lines.t: Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized.
lines.cn: 她的书中往往住着古怪、有时有罪、普遍有缺陷的怪人，而他们因为被刻画得如此丰满而变得可信。

lines.t: Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners.
lines.cn: 她的书常被描述为“风俗喜剧”。

lines.t: That is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character.
lines.cn: 也就是说，这类喜剧表现的是社会时髦圈子中流行的复杂而精致的行为准则，在那里，外表比真正的道德品格更重要。

lines.t: A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds.
lines.cn: 风俗喜剧往往奖赏聪明而诡诈的角色，而不是惩罚他们的劣行。

lines.t: The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.
lines.cn: 风俗喜剧的幽默依靠言辞机锋和戏谑调侃。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace?

options.A: It is what members use to alleviate tension in a team.
options.B: It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.
options.C: It is conducive to getting over a recession.
options.D: It is necessary for learning a new task.

questions.cn: 讲话者为什么说适应力是职场上需要具备的重要技能？

optionsCn.A: 这是团队成员用来缓解紧张的方式。
optionsCn.B: 这是雇主越来越看重的东西。
optionsCn.C: 它有利于渡过经济衰退。
optionsCn.D: 它是学习新任务的必要条件。

questions.stem: What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark?

options.A: Make better choices.
options.B: Follow innovative ideas.
options.C: Achieve recognition duly.
options.D: Accumulate work experience.

questions.cn: 根据战略顾问多丽·克拉克，适应力使我们能够做什么？

optionsCn.A: 做出更好的选择。
optionsCn.C: 及时获得认可。
optionsCn.D: 积累工作经验。

questions.stem: What do we learn about today’s work culture from the passage?

options.A: Workers show more emotional intelligence.
options.B: Workers use brains more than muscles.
options.C: People usually work flexible hours.
options.D: People often work in teams.

questions.cn: 从文章中关于当今的工作文化我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 员工表现出更高的情商。
optionsCn.C: 人们通常弹性工作。
optionsCn.D: 人们常常在团队中工作。

questions.stem: What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur?

options.A: Leave the group as soon as possible.
options.B: Anticipate setbacks well in advance.
options.C: Decide on new priorities speedily.
options.D: Stick to original goals confidently.

questions.cn: 情况发生变化时，具备适应力的员工能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 尽快离开团队。
optionsCn.C: 迅速确定新的轻重缓急。
optionsCn.D: 自信地坚持原有目标。

lines.t: Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
lines.cn: 为什么适应力是职场上需要具备的一项重要技能？

lines.t: Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.
lines.cn: 简单说，适应力是雇主越来越看重的技能。

lines.t: When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.
lines.cn: 当你花时间去学习一项新任务而不是抗拒它时，你的效率就会提高。

lines.t: You can also serve as an example to your co-workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward.
lines.cn: 你还能为那些可能难以适应的同事做个榜样，并帮助带领团队前进。

lines.t: Strategy consultant, Dorie Clark explains it to us this way: I’d say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because frankly, circumstances change-competitors introduce new products, the economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more.
lines.cn: 战略顾问多丽·克拉克这样向我们解释：我要说，适应力是职场上的一项重要技能，因为坦白讲，情况会变——竞争对手推出新产品，经济可能进入衰退，客户偏好随时间变化，等等。

lines.t: If you shake your fist at the sky and say, “Why can’t it stay the same?”, that’s not going to do very much good.
lines.cn: 如果你冲着天空挥拳喊“为什么就不能一直保持不变？”，那没什么用。

lines.t: Instead, you need to recognise when circumstances have changed, so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be.
lines.cn: 相反，你需要认清情况何时发生了改变，从而能够基于现实、而不是你希望世界怎样，去采取恰当的行动。

lines.t: That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices.
lines.cn: 这能让你做出更准确、更有依据、更有效的选择。

lines.t: Also, the workplace itself has been evolving.
lines.cn: 此外，职场本身也在演变。

lines.t: Today’s work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.
lines.cn: 如今的工作文化和管理风格往往基于团队合作，而不是僵化的等级制度。

lines.t: Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique.
lines.cn: 头脑风暴需要创造力、灵活性和情商，是一种典型的解决问题的方法。

lines.t: Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company.
lines.cn: 那些无法或不愿参与的员工，在公司里不容易有发展。

lines.t: Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too.
lines.cn: 灵活的员工还会展现出其他技能。

lines.t: They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working.
lines.cn: 情况变化时，他们能迅速重新排定轻重缓急；某件事行不通时，他们能提出额外的修改建议。

lines.t: They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.
lines.cn: 遇到挫折时，他们也能迅速重整旗鼓，自信地适应新情况而不过度反应。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What question does the speaker address in this talk?

options.A: What differentiates people from animals.
options.B: Why philosophers disagree with scientists.
options.C: Where humans’ great cognitive capacity originates.
options.D: When being creative becomes a biological mandate.

questions.cn: 讲话者在这段讲话中探讨什么问题？

optionsCn.A: 是什么把人区别于动物。
optionsCn.B: 哲学家为什么与科学家意见不一。
optionsCn.C: 人类强大的认知能力源自何处。
optionsCn.D: 创造何时成为一种生物学使命。

questions.stem: What does the speaker believe about innovation?

options.A: It is what tells apart two adjacent generations.
options.B: It is what sharpens our appetite for novelty.
options.C: It is something only geniuses can achieve.
options.D: It is something every human being can do.

questions.cn: 关于创新，讲话者相信什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是区分相邻两代人的东西。
optionsCn.B: 它激发我们对新奇的渴望。
optionsCn.C: 它是只有天才才能实现的。
optionsCn.D: 它是每个人都能做到的。

questions.stem: How does the human brain work according to the speaker?

options.A: It seeks inspiration for novel inventions.
options.B: It constantly absorbs new information.
options.C: It uses existing ideas to create new ones.
options.D: It repeats precedent on a regular basis.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，人脑是如何工作的？

optionsCn.A: 它为新颖的发明寻求灵感。
optionsCn.C: 它用已有的想法创造新的想法。
optionsCn.D: 它定期重复先例。

lines.t: What makes humans different from other species?
lines.cn: 是什么让人类与其他物种不同？

lines.t: Some philosophers argue it’s morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it’s our greater cognitive development.
lines.cn: 一些哲学家主张是道德或伦理，而一些科学家断言是我们更强的认知发展。

lines.t: But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine.
lines.cn: 但我认为，主要差别在于我们对抗常规的渴望。

lines.t: This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.
lines.cn: 这让创造成为一项生物学使命，因为我们在艺术和技术中追求的是意外，而不仅仅是对预期的满足。

lines.t: As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species.
lines.cn: 因此，狂放的想象力贯穿了我们这个物种的历史。

lines.t: We build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols, and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design.
lines.cn: 我们建造精巧的居所，为食物设计复杂的食谱，穿着反映时尚不断变化的衣服，用精心设计的标志、符号和声音交流，还乘着自己设计的机翼和轮子在各地之间往来。

lines.t: To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key.
lines.cn: 为了满足我们对新奇的渴望，创新是关键。

lines.t: But who innovates?
lines.cn: 但谁在创新？

lines.t: Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate.
lines.cn: 如今，无论外行还是专家，许多人都认为只有天才会创新。

lines.t: But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do.
lines.cn: 但我相信，创新不是只有少数人才能做的事。

lines.t: The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next.
lines.cn: 创新的驱动力存在于每个人的大脑中，而与重复性对抗所引发的，正是推动一代人与另一代人显著不同的巨变的力量。

lines.t: The drive to create the new is a trait of being human.
lines.cn: 创造新事物的驱动力是人的一种特质。

lines.t: We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions.
lines.cn: 我们成百地构建文化，成千上万地讲述新故事。

lines.t: We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not.
lines.cn: 我们创造并让自己置身于前所未有的事物之中，而动物不会。

lines.t: But where do our new ideas come from?
lines.cn: 但我们的新想法从何而来？

lines.t: According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere to great minds.
lines.cn: 许多人认为，新想法似乎不知从何而来，降临于伟大的头脑。

lines.t: From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic.
lines.cn: 从这个角度看，新想法几乎像是魔法。

lines.t: They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few.
lines.cn: 它们在灵光一闪中降临于少数被选中的人。

lines.t: However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process.
lines.cn: 然而，现实是：在人类活动的各个领域，先前的工作都在推动创造过程。

lines.t: We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it’s really the result of developing the ideas of others further.
lines.cn: 我们可能以为创新是灵感或天才的结果，但它其实是把别人的想法进一步发展出来的结果。

lines.t: This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions.
lines.cn: 这在技术领域如此：一项发明促成或激发更多发明。

lines.t: And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work.
lines.cn: 在艺术领域也如此：作家、作曲家和画家在创作中运用前人的作品。

lines.t: The human brain works from precedent.
lines.cn: 人脑是从先例出发工作的。

lines.t: We take the ideas we’ve inherited and put them together into some new shape.
lines.cn: 我们把继承来的想法拿来，重新组合成某种新的形态。

lines.t: What is a true creator?
lines.cn: 什么才是真正的创造者？

lines.t: Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing?
lines.cn: 创造者是无中生有的天才吗？

lines.t: No.
lines.cn: 不是。

lines.t: Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures.
lines.cn: 创造者只是善于运用所继承之物的人：吸收过去，并加以操作，以创造可能的未来。

lines.t: Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception.
lines.cn: 因此，人类之为创造者，是常态而非例外。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What view of many dog owners win support from researchers studying dog cognition?

options.A: Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well.
options.B: Dogs have the cognition for telling right from wrong.
options.C: Dogs have an aptitude for developing skills to interact with humans.
options.D: Dogs know when their human companions can no longer stand them.

questions.cn: 许多养狗人的哪一种看法得到了研究狗类认知的研究者的支持？

optionsCn.A: 狗知道主人身体不舒服。
optionsCn.B: 狗有辨别是非的认知能力。
optionsCn.C: 狗有发展与人类互动技能的天赋。
optionsCn.D: 狗知道它们的人类伙伴何时再也受不了它们。

questions.stem: Why can dogs detect their owner’s abnormal odor according to the speaker?

options.A: They can readily detect different ill smells of viruses.
options.B: They can easily tell what bacteria cause odor change.
options.C: They are particularly sensitive to strange smells.
options.D: They have an extremely powerful sense of smell.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，狗为什么能察觉主人异常的体味？

optionsCn.A: 它们能轻易察觉病毒引起的不同病味。
optionsCn.B: 它们容易分辨哪种细菌引起气味变化。
optionsCn.C: 它们对奇怪的气味特别敏感。
optionsCn.D: 它们有极其强大的嗅觉。

questions.stem: What does research suggest for now about dog ownership?

options.A: It can ensure owners suffer fewer chronic diseases.
options.B: It can benefit owners both physically and mentally.
options.C: It can reduce owners’ risk of getting cancer or diabetes.
options.D: It can alert owners to the seriousness of their conditions.

questions.cn: 就目前而言，研究对养狗有何建议？

optionsCn.A: 它能确保主人少得慢性病。
optionsCn.B: 它能在身体和心理两方面使主人受益。
optionsCn.C: 它能降低主人患癌症或糖尿病的风险。
optionsCn.D: 它能让主人警觉自己病情的严重性。

lines.t: Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they’re ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right.
lines.cn: 许多养狗的人都会告诉你，他们的狗不知怎的知道他们生病或心情不好；而研究狗类认知的研究者说，这些宠物主人说得没错。

lines.t: Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time.
lines.cn: 狗确实知道它们的人类伙伴什么时候过得不好。

lines.t: Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions.
lines.cn: 你的狗不仅能察觉你感冒了，家犬还表现出能够察觉小得多的情绪波动以及严重得多的身体状况。

lines.t: This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they’re familiar with, and illness causes change.
lines.cn: 这是因为狗对它们熟悉的人的变化极其敏感，而疾病会造成变化。

lines.t: If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can’t, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.
lines.cn: 例如，如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌，其体味会变得异常，而狗能闻到这种变化，即使人类闻不到，因为狗的嗅觉比人类强大得多。

lines.t: Researchers have also found that a person’s mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog’s sense of smell.
lines.cn: 研究者还发现，一个人的情绪——它可能是更大疾病的信号——会触发狗的嗅觉。

lines.t: Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well.
lines.cn: 人的情绪会以身体发出的化学信号的形式在物质层面体现出来，而狗也能闻到这些。

lines.t: Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person’s voice in order to sense changes.
lines.cn: 除了气味，狗还会从人的声音中收集信息来感知变化。

lines.t: In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain, similar to one in humans, that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker’s voice, beyond what they’d be able to pick up from familiar words alone.
lines.cn: 2014 年，研究者发现狗的大脑中有一个与人类相似的区域，使它们能理解说话者语调中的情绪线索，超出了它们仅从熟悉的词语中能捕捉到的信息。

lines.t: A person’s voice can also carry indicators of illness.
lines.cn: 人的声音也能携带疾病的信号。

lines.t: What’s not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes.
lines.cn: 而人们尚未完全弄清的是，狗对这些变化究竟理解到什么程度。

lines.t: Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn’t clear.
lines.cn: 人类会发出大量线索，但狗是否知道其中某些线索意味着疾病，并不清楚。

lines.t: What we perceive as concern on a dog’s part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.
lines.cn: 我们眼中的“狗在关心”，可能更像是好奇心增强，或是对我们哪里不对劲的怀疑，而待在你身边正是收集更多相关信息的绝佳方式。

lines.t: Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer.
lines.cn: 一些研究者断言，狗有一天会帮助医生诊断疾病，因为有些狗已经展现出察觉多种病症的能力，包括糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。

lines.t: But those researchers concede that’s probably in the distant future.
lines.cn: 但这些研究者也承认，那大概还是很遥远的事。

lines.t: For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself.
lines.cn: 就目前而言，研究表明养狗本身就有一系列好处。

lines.t: Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood.
lines.cn: 养宠物狗已被证明能增强健康、改善情绪。

lines.t: Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.
lines.cn: 狗还能帮助人放松，对慢性病患者尤其能带来慰藉。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does Onward’s report propose ministers should do?

options.A: Crack down on courses like science, technology, engineering and math.
options.B: Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students.
options.C: Look at how to reform technical and vocational education.
options.D: Ensure creative arts students get better value for money.

questions.cn: Onward 的报告提议部长们应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 打击科学、技术、工程和数学这类课程。
optionsCn.B: 限制创意艺术类课程招收新学生的能力。
optionsCn.C: 研究如何改革技术和职业教育。
optionsCn.D: 确保创意艺术类学生获得更好的回报。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think of Onward’s arguments?

options.A: Seemingly reasonable.
options.B: Clearly well-grounded.
options.C: Extremely irrational.
options.D: Apparently simplistic.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何看待 Onward 的论点？

optionsCn.A: 看似合理。
optionsCn.C: 极不合理。
optionsCn.D: 明显过于简单化。

questions.stem: What do we learn about British college graduates five years after graduation?

options.A: A high proportion of them haven’t tried to save money.
options.B: Most of them never hope to buy a house or to retire.
options.C: Forty percent of them earn less than £25,000 a year.
options.D: The majority of them have fairly well-paying jobs.

questions.cn: 关于英国大学毕业生毕业五年后的情况，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们中有很高比例的人没有尝试存钱。
optionsCn.B: 他们中的大多数人从不指望买房或退休。
optionsCn.C: 他们中有 40% 年收入低于 25,000 英镑。
optionsCn.D: 他们中大多数人拥有相当高薪的工作。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say actually accounts for the problem identified by Onward?

options.A: The context of a bank balance.
options.B: Britain’s economy as a whole.
options.C: The specific degree a student earns.
options.D: Britain’s defective educational system.

questions.cn: 讲话者说 Onward 指出的问题实际上是什么造成的？

optionsCn.A: 银行存款的情境。
optionsCn.C: 学生所获得的特定学位。
optionsCn.D: 英国有缺陷的教育制度。

lines.t: Earlier this month, the think-tank called Onward published a report, “A Question of Degree”, which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money.
lines.cn: 本月早些时候，名为“Onward”的智库发布了一份报告《学位问题》，主张创意艺术类学位不值这些钱。

lines.t: Ministers, according to Onward, should “crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation”, restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold.
lines.cn: 据 Onward 所说，部长们应当“打击那些在学生毕业十年后为其提供的价值极其有限的课程”，如果毕业生的平均收入低于学生贷款还款门槛，就限制这类课程招收新学生。

lines.t: Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favoured.
lines.cn: 像科学、技术、工程、数学以及经济学这样毕业生平均收入较高的课程，则应受到优待。

lines.t: The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money.
lines.cn: 该报告为一项政府评估提供了洞见，该评估探讨如何改革技术教育、以及如何确保学生获得良好的回报。

lines.t: At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.
lines.cn: 乍一看，Onward 的说法甚至似乎有道理。

lines.t: According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than £25,000 a year, ten years after graduation.
lines.cn: 根据他们的数据，大多数创意艺术类学生在毕业十年后年收入低于 25,000 英镑。

lines.t: The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university.
lines.cn: 事实上，创意艺术类男生平均收入明显低于他们如果根本没上过大学的收入。

lines.t: This isn’t really good for anyone, and it’s certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
lines.cn: 这对谁都不太好，对毕业生当然更没有好处——他们被迫忍受一种永远存不下钱、买不起房、也别指望退休的生活方式。

lines.t: Onward have identified a real problem.
lines.cn: Onward 指出了一个真实的问题。

lines.t: Creative arts graduates from top universities-like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students-have fairly good work prospects, while 40 percent of all graduates-regardless of their degree-are on less than £25,000 a year, five years after graduation.
lines.cn: 来自顶尖大学——比如私立教育学生比例很高的牛津——的创意艺术类毕业生，工作前景相当不错；而所有毕业生中，无论什么学位，都有 40% 在毕业五年后年收入低于 25,000 英镑。

lines.t: This suggests that the problem isn’t really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.
lines.cn: 这表明问题其实并不在于特定学生学习特定学位，而在于整个经济。

lines.t: Regardless of what they’ve studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they’re lucky enough to be born with successful parents.
lines.cn: 无论学的是什么，年轻人很难出人头地，除非他们有幸生于成功的家庭。

lines.t: If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world.
lines.cn: 如果部长们想让教育为年轻人带来回报，他们需要超越高等教育领域，看向更广阔的世界。

lines.t: The rewards that education gives us are not measurable.
lines.cn: 教育给予我们的回报是无法量化的。

lines.t: They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct.
lines.cn: 它们并不总是立刻显现，当然也不总是直接的。

lines.t: An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn’t received it.
lines.cn: 教育会让你变成一个与未曾接受它时不同的自己。

lines.t: We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life.
lines.cn: 我们应当从人生的角度、而不是从银行存款的角度，去看教育的价值。

lines.t: If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of “value for money”, we will all be made poorer as a result.
lines.cn: 如果我们继续任由自己被“物有所值”的论调牵着走，我们所有人都会因此变得更贫乏。
